title: ICU 72h readmission model - governed weekly retraining

root_goal.statement: Keep the deployed ICU 72-hour readmission prediction model clinically useful and safe on FUTURE patients: replace the production model only when a candidate is shown better on time-forward data it never saw, without harming calibration, subgroups or alert burden.
root_goal.observable_success: Over a prospective monitoring window, the deployed model's AUC, calibration (slope/intercept, Brier) and PPV at the operating threshold, computed on actually observed 72h readmissions of patients admitted AFTER the model was frozen, are non-inferior or better than the previous champion, with no subgroup degradation beyond the frozen margin; every production swap has a signed human approval record and a rollback path.
out_of_scope: Training and scoring AUC on the same month of data (in-sample AUC is not evidence of improvement)
Automatic production replacement without human approval
Changing the readmission label definition, the 72h window, the holdout protocol or acceptance thresholds by the training agent
Direct clinical decisions or treatment changes driven by the model
Using patient data beyond the approved ICU data-use scope

classification_rationale: The brief as written is a single self-scoring loop: the trainer is evaluated on the same month it trained on, so AUC almost always rises (in-sample overfitting/leakage) and an auto-swap would push a worse model into a clinical system. AUC is gameable and alone ignores calibration, subgroup harm and alert burden; production replacement is a high-risk side effect; label maturity (72h outcomes) and data drift operate at slower cadences than weekly training. This needs an execution loop plus an independent time-forward verifier grounded in a frozen anchor the trainer cannot touch, a counter-metric loop, a monthly audit of the data pipeline and live performance, arbitration, and a human deployment gate -> graph_plus_loop.

allowed_actions: Read de-identified ICU training window (admissions up to the training cutoff)
Train candidate models in the sandbox within frozen feature/label definitions
Write candidate model artifacts and training reports to the candidate registry
Propose changes to thresholds, windows or features as a written proposal
Deploy an approved candidate to shadow mode
Roll back to the previous champion on a monitoring alarm
forbidden_actions: Read or query the time-forward holdout labels from the training loop
Evaluate a candidate on its own training data and report that as acceptance
Replace the production model without a signed human approval
Modify the label definition, holdout split, evaluation code or acceptance thresholds
Delete or overwrite the previous champion model

frozen_rules: Training window and evaluation window never overlap: candidates are scored only on admissions after the training cutoff plus a >=72h label-maturity gap (time-forward holdout).
Readmission label = unplanned ICU readmission within 72h of ICU discharge, taken from the ADT/EHR record; definition frozen.

Acceptance: holdout AUC improvement >= frozen margin with bootstrap CI lower bound > 0 versus champion on the SAME holdout, AND calibration slope within 0.8-1.2, AND no prespecified subgroup AUC drop > 0.03, AND alert rate change within +/-20%.
Evaluation code, holdout set and thresholds are versioned and write-protected from the training loop.
Every production swap requires Bruce's signed approval after shadow mode; previous champion stays available for rollback.
Agents may only propose changes to goals, anchors, thresholds, permissions or frozen rules; applying them requires human approval.

failure_policy.failed: Candidate rejected; champion stays in production; rejection reason logged; next weekly cycle proceeds.
failure_policy.blocked: If the holdout anchor is stale, label data incomplete, or drift audit fails, freeze retraining/deployment and escalate to Bruce.
failure_policy.budget_exhausted: Stop the cycle, keep champion, hand off training report and open questions to Bruce.

conditions: completed: candidate passed verification and counter-metrics, shadow mode OK, Bruce approved swap, prospective monitoring confirms non-inferiority
failed: candidate rejected by verifier or counter-metric veto; champion retained
blocked: anchor stale, label pipeline broken, drift or data-scope issue; escalated to Bruce
budget_exhausted: retries or cost exceeded; stop and hand off

arbitration.priority_policy: Patient safety and calibration/subgroup fairness > prospective real-world performance > time-forward holdout AUC gain > training speed/freshness. Any veto from verifier or counter-metric loop blocks the swap; ties resolved by keeping the champion.

verification.independence_statement: The verifier is a separate deterministic evaluation service with fresh context, using frozen evaluation code and a time-forward holdout of admissions after the training cutoff whose labels come directly from the ADT/EHR outcome record maintained by the hospital data team; the training loop cannot read, select or rewrite this holdout or the evaluation code. Evaluator and data provenance both differ from the trainer.

anchors.source: Hospital ADT/EHR readmission outcomes for ICU admissions after the training cutoff (+72h label maturity), extracted by the data team
anchors.evidence_form: Versioned, hash-locked time-forward holdout with observed 72h readmission labels
anchors.freshness_rule: Rebuilt weekly from the newest matured admissions; holdout older than 35 days is stale and blocks evaluation

nodes.responsibility: Weekly retrain candidate on the rolling training window ending at the cutoff; report in-sample metrics only as diagnostics
Provide frozen, write-protected time-forward holdout with real observed 72h readmission outcomes
Score candidate and champion on the same time-forward holdout with frozen code; bootstrap CI of AUC difference; veto if acceptance not met
Check calibration, Brier, subgroup AUC gaps (age, sex, admission type, unit), PPV and alert rate at operating threshold, leakage/feature audit; veto cheap AUC wins
Combine verifier and counter-metric verdicts under frozen priority policy; any veto keeps champion
nodes.priority_policy: Safety/calibration/subgroup > prospective performance > holdout AUC gain > freshness; any veto blocks

nodes.responsibility: Bruce reviews evidence and shadow-mode results and signs or rejects production swap
After signed approval, promote candidate from shadow to production, keep previous champion for rollback
Monthly audit of label pipeline, data drift, feature leakage, and prospective performance of the deployed model on actual outcomes; trigger rollback or freeze
Quarterly review of goal, thresholds, windows, subgroups; agents may only propose, Bruce approves changes
Bruce approves or rejects proposed changes to anchor, holdout protocol, thresholds or label definition
Record terminal state (completed/failed/blocked/budget_exhausted) and hand off to Bruce
